solver: cmd/solve, three arms over the same 8 instances. A = -cand-mode off (legacy brute-force enumeration, HEAD-equivalent), B = -cand-mode mix -cand-hop-cache=true, C = -cand-mode mix -cand-hop-cache=false. All other flags identical: -rounds 150 -wall-sec 90 -hot-k 6 -peel 6 -model twin -budget-mode full -presolve unmovable -presolve-time 15 -presolve-deep 100 -skip-floor=true.
why: The candidate layer (internal/cand) had been landed and unit-tested but never measured end-to-end against the legacy generator it replaces, and the hop cache (internal/hops) had never been measured in the outer loop rather than in isolation. This experiment answers both: does the targeted generator beat brute force, and does the per-banned-set BFS cache pay for itself.

arms.A: legacy brute-force enumeration: every node as waypoint, ranked by relief, top-12 per demand per family
arms.B: cand mix (hot_center + od_scan + bottleneck, round-robin merged) with hops.Cache enabled -- the shipping path
arms.C: same generator with hops.Cache.SetEnabled(false): recomputes every BFS, the uncached control

noise_floor.measurement: three byte-identical B-config runs on setA-10 gave firstbit 141304 / 152173 / 152173, a 7.7% spread
noise_floor.source: Gurobi, not presolve and not the cache: the spread persists with -presolve off -rounds 60 (152174/152173/152173/152173 alternating cache on/off). internal/mip/mip.go:362 sets a TimeLimit on EVERY peel layer, so a time-limited layer returns the incumbent at an arbitrary wall moment.
noise_floor.instance_dependent: setA-06 is fully reproducible in both arms (B 101408 x3, A 105633 x2), so its 4.0% win is real; setA-10 is not.
noise_floor.methodological_consequence: single-run firstbit differences below ~8% are not conclusions. Either repeat to reproducibility or measure with Gurobi removed from the loop (cmd/candbench).

cache_neutrality_correction.wrong_earlier_inference: tabulate_cand_ab.py originally reported the B/C disagreement on setA-10/19 as 'the cache is not pure memoisation, a bug'.
cache_neutrality_correction.why_wrong: The cache is pure at the candidate-generator level (candbench: 20/20 instances bit-identical candidate lists). At the OUTER-LOOP level B and C may still differ because each round runs a wall-clock-dependent Gurobi MIP, and the cache changes the timing. A B/C disagreement in the outer loop is a noise indicator, not evidence of impurity.
cache_neutrality_correction.action_taken: scripts/tabulate_cand_ab.py (and the copy in data/) now states this and recommends cmd/candbench for cache-purity checks. Verified the corrected script reproduces the same table.
